messages:
Jordan (Eng): Hey team — planning a 10-week stint in Portugal starting mid‑June. Still on US payroll. Quick Qs: am I eligible for the WFH stipend while abroad? Any company tax/nexus risk if I’m ~70% in Lisbon during that period? Also want to ship my standing desk there — reimbursement rules?

Anya (People Ops): Congrats! Short answers: yes, you can get a pro‑rated WFH stipend while temporarily abroad; shipping may be reimbursable with pre‑approval. Please file the temporary remote/hub form and include dates + shipping estimate. :+1:

Jordan (Eng): Got it. What exactly goes on the form and who signs?

Anya (People Ops): The form asks: block dates, location, expected % time abroad, hardware being shipped, manager signoff. Manager sign + People Ops review required. If duration >= 90 days we trigger payroll/localization automatically; 10 weeks is under 90 but >30 so Legal does a quick check. Tagging @Sanjay for legal review.

Sanjay (Legal): Quick legal note: Personal tax/residency and payroll withholding are the main risks for the individual (e.g., 183-day rules). Company nexus risk for a single short-term employee is generally low, but depends on repeated visits, whether you host customers or open an office, etc. For 70% over 10 weeks the usual outcome is no corporate nexus, but we still run a short check. Please mark the submission as "temporary remote" so Legal can review. :warning:

Jordan (Eng): For the stipend — is it the standard $100/mo pro-rated, or a different amount when abroad? And shipping — any caps?

Anya (People Ops): If your homebase remains US you get the standard stipend amount pro-rated by days in the month and converted if we need to pay locally. For shipping: submit receipts, but we require People Ops pre‑approval for shipping >$500. I can pre‑approve up to $600 in your case if you include quotes.

Liam (Payroll): Note from payroll: if you stay on US payroll we maintain USD stipend payments. If Legal flags localization, payroll transition can cause change/delay. We also need up‑to‑date tax docs (W‑9/W‑8 as applicable) if your tax residency changes. Fill the form now so we have time to check before travel.

PeopleOps Bot: Temporary remote/HUB form: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/temp-remote-form
Policy summary: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/policies/temp-remote
Automation note: duration >= 90d -> auto triggers payroll/localization workflow.

Jordan (Eng): Helpful — thanks. I’ll mark 70% and add exact block dates (7 weeks in Lisbon, 3 weeks back in US across the 10-week window).

Anya (People Ops): Perfect. Include "bringing standing desk" and estimated ship cost. We’ll tag it as "short-term EU" and run Legal + Payroll checks.

Sanjay (Legal): We’ll review within 48 hours of form submission. If anything looks like potential nexus or dependent contractor risk we’ll reach out. For Portugal specifically: personal tax/residency triggers at 183 days in a calendar year; company PE risk still low for a single short-term headcount, but we’ll confirm. :mag:

Jordan (Eng): Filing now. Will @Anya DM shipping quotes and manager sign-off after I get them.

Anya (People Ops): Got it. I’ll confirm stipend proration and pre‑approve desk ship up to $600 once receipts/quotes are attached. Expect an update in 48–72 business hours after submission. :sparkles:

PeopleOps Bot: Form received: ID TR-2026-0457. Next steps: manager sign-off -> People Ops review -> Legal/Payroll if flagged. ETA: 48–72 hrs.
